newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Former Zaire premier appears after trek to safety.
newsitem.headline: Former Zaire premier appears after trek to safety.

text.p: Zaire's former prime minister, Faustin Birindwa, has arrived in the capital Kinshasa after fleeing on foot into the bush when rebels seized his eastern hometown of Bukavu two weeks ago.

He went to Bukavu two days before it fell, saying he wanted to be with his people. But he had not expected the rapid collapse of the Zairean army stationed there and was forced to walk four days through the wilderness to escape.
"At a certain moment a number of my friends had been killed, including the archbishop of Bukavu, and the hotel which I own had been bombarded by rockets," he said in a weekend interview with Reuters.
"I could not remain in the ruins while all the neighbourhoods were emptying. I had to save my own life," he added.
Birindwa said he saw the corpses of hundreds of Zairean soldiers as well as civilians before he left.
"It made me sick at heart to see the number of dead bodies on the streets of Bukavu, in particular in front of the gendamerie where all the guards were slaughtered."

Thousands of poorly equipped Zairean soldiers together with Rwandan Hutu militias fled Bukavu in disarray when heavily armed rebels backed by the Rwandan Patriotic Army entered the town on October 29.
The defeated forces fled after looting Bukavu clean, taking all remaining vehicles, including dozens stolen from international aid agencies.

Birindwa fled on foot along with several employees of his hotel, three days after the army was routed, joining the hundreds of thousands of Zaireans and some 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees now displaced throughout the region.
He said on his tortuous journey through the bush the only sign of continuing resistance to the rebellion was from Rwandan and Burundian Hutu militias manning roadblocks.
Birindwa walked across more than 100 km (60 miles) of rugged mountain terrain to reach the village of Kamitoga from where he was flown out in a small plane piloted by his son.
